cases.prompt: Three annotators labelled 500 Northwind Billing Assistant messages with intents for our eval set. Are the labels reliable enough to use?
expected: Runs scripts/agreement.py on item_id,annotator,label rows; reports Krippendorff's alpha first, with kappas
Labels interpretation bands as conventions (Landis & Koch; Krippendorff 0.667/0.800)
Asks the data owner for the minimum alpha rather than choosing one; lists disputed items and guideline gaps

cases.prompt: Each item was labelled by one person. What's our inter-annotator agreement?
expected: Says agreement cannot be computed without 2+ independent ratings per item; recommends double-labelling a sample; reports no score

cases.prompt: Measure agreement on the Northwind intent labels against our guidelines; we need alpha of at least 0.5.
expected: alpha 0.595 passes 0.5; Fleiss n/a (2 and 3 ratings per item); 7 disputed items; plan_change is a low-agreement label not in the guidelines

checks.check: contains:"Low-agreement labels the guidelines do not mention: `plan_change`."

cases.prompt: Check our annotators' agreement.
expected: Asks once for the labels CSV

cases.prompt: We don't have written guidelines; just tell me which labels are defined well.
expected: Guideline coverage is TBD for the Annotation lead; no gate applied; no definition status invented

checks.check: contains:"plan_change,6,0.500,[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]"
contains:"No minimum agreement set ([TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]); no gate applied."

cases.prompt: Gate the Northwind labels: fail unless alpha is at least 0.667.
expected: alpha 0.595 < 0.667 → FAIL, exit 1, outputs still written

checks.check: contains:"**FAIL** — alpha 0.595 is below the minimum 0.667"

cases.prompt: Agreement for labels where each item had one annotator.
expected: Exit 1 with a clear error; no alpha or kappa reported

checks.check: contains:"**No agreement score: no item has ratings from 2 or more annotators"

cases.prompt: We revised the guidelines after the pilot and relabelled. Did agreement improve on the Northwind intent labels? Here is the pilot's agreement result.
expected: Reads the pilot agreement.json: alpha 0.321 -> 0.595 (improved), disputed items 12 -> 7, every label at or above its pilot agreement; gate at 0.5 passes

cases.prompt: Before we calibrate our LLM-as-judge, 4 reviewers rated 300 chatbot replies as pass / partial / fail. Our eval owner set a minimum alpha of 0.8. Write up the agreement check; I'll export the ratings later.
expected: Summary gate line states the 0.8 minimum against alpha [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]; no alpha, kappa or count is printed
Says to export one row per rating as item_id, annotator, label and run scripts/agreement.py
Method & limits say ratings must be independent and that agreement measures consistency, not correctness

cases.prompt: Clinical coders labelled 1,200 discharge notes into 6 categories. Most notes had 2 coders; a 150-note sample had 3. Which agreement statistics should we report?
expected: Krippendorff's alpha (nominal) is the headline because it handles different numbers of ratings per item
Fleiss' kappa is reported n/a with the reason (items have 2 and 3 ratings)
Pairwise Cohen's kappa per coder pair and percent agreement are included; no values are invented

cases.prompt: Overall percent agreement on our review-sentiment labels was 0.78. Per label: positive 0.90 (defined in guidelines), negative 0.85 (defined), neutral 0.81 (defined), mixed 0.55 (not defined), sarcastic 0.40 (not defined). Which labels does the guideline need to clarify?
expected: Guideline gaps are mixed and sarcastic: both below overall percent agreement (0.78) and not defined in the guidelines
Positive, negative and neutral are not listed as gaps
Recommends boundary rules for the top confusion pairs and re-labelling a fresh sample after the guideline change

cases.prompt: Pairwise Cohen's kappa between our three raters came out 0.58, 0.63 and 0.71. Is that good?
expected: Maps the values with Landis & Koch: 0.58 moderate; 0.63 and 0.71 substantial
Labels the bands as conventions, not statistical tests
Recommends Krippendorff's alpha as the headline and leaves the pass threshold to the data owner

cases.prompt: Trust & safety pilot: 3 moderators independently labelled 200 posts with 5 policy labels using our draft guidelines. We plan to label 50k posts next month. What should the agreement report look like before we scale?
expected: Gives the report skeleton in order: Summary, Agreement, Disputed items, Guideline gaps, Method & limits
Gate line says no minimum is set and asks the data owner for it rather than choosing one
Disputed items go to an adjudicator and the guideline is sharpened before labelling at scale

cases.prompt: Annotators rated answer helpfulness on a 1-5 scale. Can you give me weighted kappa for that?
expected: Says this skill handles nominal labels only; ordinal or interval scales are out of scope
Explains that treating 1-5 as categories ignores distance (4 vs 5 counts the same as 1 vs 5)
Does not report a weighted kappa as if computed

cases.prompt: Our two labellers sat side by side, agreed each label out loud, then each typed it into the tool. Alpha came out 0.97. Can we call the labels reliable?
expected: Flags that ratings were not independent, so agreement is inflated and 0.97 does not show reliability
Recommends an independent re-label of a sample before using the labels
